chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Najih, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:
There is no harm in the Muhrim (person in Ihram) wearing a ring.

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a pilgrim in Ihram to wear a ring?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani’s *al-Istibsar* clarifies that wearing a ring (khatam) is permissible for a muhrim, distinguishing it from other garments or items that are explicitly prohibited during Ihram. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling highlights the principle that not all forms of adornment or utility are forbidden, but only those specifically enumerated in the sacred texts or derived by analogy (qiyas) to the prohibited categories. The narration underscores the precision required in distinguishing between permissible accessories and those that constitute a violation of the sanctity of the pilgrimage state.
